signature.name: Christ of El Picacho
signature.detail: The towering statue of Christ overlooking Tegucigalpa is the city's most recognizable sight and the top landmark for first-time visitors. Go early in the morning or late afternoon for clearer views and cooler air, and bring a light layer since the hilltop can be breezy.

signature.name: Basílica de Suyapa
signature.detail: This basilica is the country's most important religious site and draws pilgrims year-round, making it a cultural must-see. Dress modestly out of respect, and visit on a weekday morning to avoid the largest crowds.

signature.name: Parque Nacional La Tigra
signature.detail: A cloud forest park just outside the city offers hiking and a cool escape from the urban heat. Arrive early, wear sturdy shoes, and consider going with a guide since trails can be muddy.

signature.name: Museum of National Identity (MIN)
signature.detail: This museum gives a compact overview of Honduran history and culture, useful for context before exploring the city. Check opening hours in advance, as schedules can vary.

signature.name: Valle de Ángeles
signature.detail: A traditional village in the hills near Tegucigalpa known for crafts and a relaxed atmosphere. It makes an easy half-day trip; go on a weekend for the liveliest market scene.
